rationale: The static profile is empty (no source files, line counts, or function inventory), so this is McCat 08-main, a small MultiSource C driver program with few, short-lived functions and modest loop bodies; that favors cheap, composable transformations over heavy ones. SUB is weighted highest since instruction substitution is near-free at runtime and gives broad baseline diversity, with SPLIT and BCF next to break up and obscure control flow; FLA is kept moderately weighted because flattening is effective against static control-flow analysis but carries the largest runtime cost, so only functions whose features clearly favor SecurityGain should receive it. IBR and ICALL get moderate security/diversity weights with tempered runtime weights since opaque predicates and indirect calls add per-execution overhead on a benchmark often run with tight timing loops. IGV is weighted lowest and its CorrectnessRisk weight kept highest because indirecting global variable access interacts badly with link-time and ABI assumptions in small driver programs that may rely on externally visible globals, and its marginal diversity gain does not justify that risk. All CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.4 overall, keeping the selection biased toward provably safe transformations to preserve correctness while still spreading DiversityGain across all seven passes so no two functions receive identical obfuscation stacks.
